items.label: 6. 中心优势转化王翼进攻（西班牙开局）
items.label_en: 6. Turning a Central Advantage into a Kingside Attack (Ruy Lopez)
items.explanation_en: The Ruy Lopez builds a strong center patiently: Bb5 pressures the c6-knight defending e5, then c3 prepares d4. After development and castling, White establishes the full pawn center and advances d5 to lock it, gaining space for a kingside attack. The key lesson is that central control can be built gradually and converted into an attack rather than exchanged immediately.

items.label: 7. 弃兵换中心控制权（国王弃兵）
items.label_en: 7. Gambiting a Pawn for Central Control (King's Gambit)
items.explanation_en: In the King's Gambit, White offers the f-pawn to gain time, open the e-file, and establish a central pawn duo quickly with d4. The compensation is rapid development and attacking space, but White's kingside becomes less secure and the position demands precise play. Compared with the slower Ruy Lopez, White can build the center sooner by accepting this risk.

items.label: 8. 封闭中心后侧翼突破（国王印度防御）
items.label_en: 8. Flank Breaks After the Center Closes (King's Indian Defense)
items.explanation_en: The King's Indian shows a different approach to the center: Black allows White to occupy it, then closes it with ...e5 and challenges on the wings. After d5, White can seek a queenside break with c4-c5, while Black attacks on the kingside with ...f5-f4. Once the center is locked, flank space and open lines become the main battleground.

items.label: 9. 中心压制速胜（四马开局）
items.label_en: 9. Rapid Central Pressure (Four Knights Game)
items.explanation_en: In the Four Knights Game, White chooses an early d4 to challenge the center directly, then recaptures and uses the pieces to occupy strong central squares. Exchanges can damage Black's pawn structure and leave White with more active pieces. This plan establishes central control quickly, but requires accurate calculation because the position opens early.

items.label: 10. 忽视中心的代价（反面教材）
items.label_en: 10. The Cost of Ignoring the Center (A Cautionary Example)
items.explanation_en: This deliberately poor example shows White spending several moves on flank pawns while leaving the center untouched. Black occupies d5 and e5, develops naturally, and gains space and active lines; the resulting central control leads to a dangerous passed pawn and a kingside invasion. The contrast makes the opening principle clear: flank moves that ignore the center can leave the opponent in control of the whole game.

categories.label: A2 控制中心
categories.label_en: A2 Piece Pressure on the Center

items.label: 6. 观察每步如何让轻子控制格子越来越多（伦敦体系）
items.label_en: 6. Accumulating Piece Control (London System)
items.explanation_en: The London System demonstrates how each move can add control of central squares. Nf3 controls e5 and d4; d4 occupies the center; Bf4 and later Bg3 add pressure on e5; and the other pieces reinforce the structure. The final Ne5 outpost crowns the gradual accumulation of control.

items.label: 7. Bb5没有直接占中心，却做了什么（西班牙开局）
items.label_en: 7. Bb5's Indirect Control (Ruy Lopez)
items.explanation_en: In the Ruy Lopez, Bb5 does not occupy a central square or directly attack e5. It targets the c6-knight, the pawn's defender, thereby indirectly pressuring e5. The bishop's retreats maintain that threat while White prepares d4.

items.label: 8. 双方都用子力控中心，谁更协调谁占优（英格兰对称）
items.label_en: Comparing Coordinated Piece Control (Symmetrical English)
items.explanation_en: Both sides use pawns and pieces to influence the center in a symmetrical English Opening. The lesson is that the quality and coordination of control matter more than simply counting pieces: Be6 is more active than Bd2 and creates a more useful setup.

items.label: 9. Bg2斜线加c4，兵的占领与子的控制完美结合（卡塔兰）
items.label_en: Combining Occupation and Piece Control (Catalan)
items.explanation_en: The Catalan combines central occupation and piece control: the d4-pawn occupies the center, c4 influences d5, and the fianchettoed bishop on g2 controls the long diagonal. These layers reinforce one another and make Black's counterplay difficult.

items.label: 10. 轻子走边路，中心格彻底失控（反面教材）
items.label_en: Flank Knights Lose the Center (Cautionary Example)
items.explanation_en: This cautionary example shows the cost of developing both knights to the edge. White gives up central control, while Black occupies the center, develops, and later exploits the exposed kingside. The misplaced knights become targets and White's pawn structure is damaged.

items.label: 6. 判断空间差，对比双方活动区域（卡罗坎推进）
items.label_en: 6. Comparing Space and Activity (Caro-Kann Advance)
items.explanation_en: In the Caro-Kann Advance, White's e5-pawn restricts Black's pieces. Compare the ranks and squares available to each side, then watch Black use ...c5 to challenge d4, open lines, and seek counterplay. Track how each move changes the available space.

items.label: 7. 步步为营扩展，每步兵推进有子力支撑（后翼弃兵）
items.label_en: 7. Supported Expansion (Queen's Gambit Declined)
items.explanation_en: This Queen's Gambit Declined example shows White expanding step by step with piece support. The moves develop pieces, reinforce d4, and prepare e4 rather than advancing pawns prematurely. Black's ...dxc4 and ...Nd5 create active counterplay, showing that space must be challenged, not merely endured.

items.label: 8. 双向空间竞赛，找出白方f4冒进漏洞（西西里龙式）
items.label_en: A Two-Wing Space Race (Sicilian Dragon)
items.explanation_en: In the Sicilian Dragon, White seeks kingside space with f4-f5 while Black expands on the queenside with ...b5-b4. Evaluate whether f4 is supported by the center and developed pieces, and compare the timing of both flank plans.

items.label: 9. 被压制时如何突围，找到c5关键解脱步（法国防御）
items.label_en: Breaking Out with ...c5 (French Defense)
items.explanation_en: In the French Defense, Black's pawn chain can restrict the pieces, especially the bishop on c8. The ...c5 break challenges d4 and gives Black a choice: close the center or open lines for active counterplay. The lesson is to seek a freeing break rather than defend passively.

items.label: 10. f5是安全还是冒进？判断空间推进时机（国王印度）
items.label_en: Is ...f5 Safe or Overextended? (King's Indian)
items.explanation_en: Evaluate Black's ...f5 advance using three factors: the central structure, the king's safety, and piece support. In this position the center is closed, Black has castled, and pieces are ready to support the pawn advance. Compare this with positions where an open center or an uncastled king would make ...f5 risky.

categories.label: A4 线路控制
categories.label_en: A4 Control of Files and Diagonals

items.label: 6. 弃子打开d线，车入侵d7赢后（菲利多尔防御）
items.label_en: 6. Open the d-File with a Sacrifice (Philidor Defense)
items.explanation_en: White clears the d-file with exchanges and sacrifices, then castles long to place a rook on the open file. Immediate penetration to d7 wins material. The lesson is to open a line, occupy it at once, and use it before the opponent can reorganize.

items.label: 7. 用兑换主动打开线路（卡洛卡恩兑换变体）
items.label_en: 7. Open a File Through Exchanges (Caro-Kann Exchange)
items.explanation_en: White exchanges a bishop for a knight to reduce the blockers on the e-file, then places a rook there immediately. The exchange is valuable because it creates a route for the rook to pressure Black's central weaknesses.

items.label: 8. 封闭对方线路——d5兵封锁d线（尼姆佐印度防御）
items.label_en: 8. Block the Opponent's File with d5 (Nimzo-Indian)
items.explanation_en: After Black opens the d-file to activate the pieces, White advances d5 to block the file. The pawn wall restricts Black's rooks and knights while giving White a space advantage. Proactively closing an opponent's active line can be as important as opening one for yourself.

items.label: 9. Re1占e线，瞄准第5横线渗透（意大利开局）
items.label_en: 9. Pre-Occupy the e-File with Re1 (Italian Game)
items.explanation_en: White places a rook on the e-file before it opens. The rook is ready to become active immediately after a central exchange, illustrating the strategy of pre-controlling a file instead of waiting to claim it later.

items.label: 10. 纵线+斜线联合——Re1与Bc2构建立体控制（西班牙封闭）
items.label_en: 10. Coordinate a File and Diagonal (Closed Ruy Lopez)
items.explanation_en: White combines Re1 on the e-file with Bc2 on the c2-h7 diagonal. The rook pressures e5 directly while the bishop supports the attack from another line, creating coordinated threats that are harder to defend.
